title: Ahi tuna on crispy rice
equipment: Cast-iron or other heavy skillet (for searing)

items: 1 cup sushi rice (short-grain), rinsed until the water runs clear
8 oz sushi-grade ahi tuna steak, about 1 inch thick, kept cold until cooking
2 Tbsp sesame seeds (white, black or a mix)
½ cup neutral oil (such as canola or avocado), divided
1 jalapeño, sliced into very thin rounds

steps: Combine the rice and 1¼ cups water in the saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Rest off the heat, covered, 10 min.

Stir the vinegar, sugar and ½ tsp salt into the warm rice. While it's still warm, press it firmly into the lined pan in an even layer about ¾ inch thick, using wet hands or the bottom of a cup. Cover and chill at least 1 hr, until firm.
Lift the rice out by the plastic and cut it into 16 squares, about 2 inches each. Wipe the knife with a damp towel between cuts.

Heat ¼ cup oil in the nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the squares in batches, 3–4 min per side, until deep golden and crisp, adding more oil as needed. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Pat the tuna dry, season it with salt and press sesame seeds onto all sides. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the heavy skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Sear the tuna 30–45 sec per side, until the seeds are toasted and only the outer ⅛ inch turns opaque.
Move the tuna to a cutting board and slice it against the grain about ¼ inch thick.
Top each rice square with a slice of avocado, a slice of tuna and a jalapeño round. Spoon a little ponzu over each and scatter with scallions. Serve right away while the rice is crisp.
tips: The tuna is served rare, so buy fish sold as sushi-grade or for raw eating. Keep it in the fridge until the minute you sear it and serve within 30 min.
Press the rice while it's warm. Cold rice won't stick together and the squares fall apart in the pan.
Make the rice block up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Fry it just before serving.
storage: Doesn't keep. The rice loses its crunch and the tuna is rare, so eat it the day you make it. Only the uncut, unfried rice block keeps, up to 1 day in the fridge.
